docs.title: Sankhara
docs.text:
Sankhara follows a people from a small band at their first fires to whatever they become, lived one person at a time. Each turn is a year. You act as one character, with a few slots of attention and the means your place among the people gives you: what is held in common if you lead, your family's if you hunt, gather or keep the songs. Some things take years; events arrive, some of them asking something of you.

The ideas behind it are in Concepts; how they are built is in Architecture.

Status

Playable: a band of a few hundred people, yearly turns, multi-year undertakings you can let run, a web of discoveries whose forms the people settle on, roles that appear as the people change, and other peoples to meet. Policy and more development come in Milestone 2; detailed NPC relationships and politics in Milestone 3.

docs.title: Running
docs.text:
uv sync
uv run sankhara        # or: uv run python -m sankhara

Choose New Game, then Let the years pass: the years run on their own until you pause them, and you can change the pace. Click a slot under Your attention whenever you want to take something up; you can also leave all of them free. One year steps through a single year. The game saves itself every year; Continue picks up where you left off.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
All code lives in the sankhara package under src/. The game is split into a pure-Python simulation (sankhara.sim, no Kivy, fully unit-tested and saveable) and a UI (sankhara.ui) that only reads state and calls a handful of game functions.

Package Responsibility sankhara.sim The game: state, rules, the yearly loop, lives and save/load. sankhara.world Map generation (map_gen.py) and hex-grid math (hexgrid.py). sankhara.core game_engine.generate_map(seed) builds the terrain. sankhara.entities Name generation per culture (namer.py). sankhara.ui Kivy screens: menu, game view (with the chooser, "What we know" and the choice of a custom's form), between-lives screen; theme.py palette and widgets; words.py turns numbers into the words the player sees. sankhara.constants config.py: map size, noise, biome thresholds and resources, culture groups. sankhara.app SankharaApp: screen flow and autosave.

docs.title: How the design maps to code
docs.text:
The design lives in Concepts. After the first play-through the game starts with a small band rather than a kingdom; this is how that is built:

Design Implementation One turn is one year game.end_year() advances the world one year, then begin_year() sets up the next. 2–3 slots of personal attention stations.ACTION_SLOTS = 3. game.options() offers three groups (Option.group): matters at hand (each EventInstance with answers, action ids open to the player's role; events.offer() fills them and marks the matter expected when the role has a plain duty in it), the people's works (projects.py; one of each kind of new work, aimed where it is needed most) and your own (personal projects and the lasting cares, Action.care). Nothing is chosen for the player: slots start free, a care is kept up until changed, an answer is kept up while its matter recurs (plan keys a:<matter key>:<action> are stable across years), and a project's slot goes free when it ends (game.begin_year, replan). Lead from wherever you are Most projects are the people's works (Project.common). Finishing one earns its leader and helpers regard (FINISH_REGARD, HELPED_REGARD), so serving the people is the road to leading them. Anyone can begin one with their own means (at half cost; slower; camp works only at their own camp unless they lead), help with one someone else leads (each helper adds work), take up one left unfinished, or call others to it (rally: spends standing to add support, which adds work and draws NPC helpers). NPCs join works more readily when the one leading is respected or liked. When a leader dies or sets a work aside it passes to a helper, the people's leader or an elder (projects.pass_on), or waits for someone. A custom being settled lets anyone speak for a form; a respected voice weighs more (game.choose_form, pending_mode). The thread between lives Works an earlier character of the player's worked on stay in play: the birth screen lists what was finished while the new character grew up and what is still unfinished and who carries it (game.thread_lines), and the chooser marks those works. GameState.legacy remembers finished works and settled customs the player had a hand in; the end-of-life screen shows them. Years that run on their own "Let the years pass" runs a clock (GameView._tick, PACES): a year lasts a few seconds, shown by a bar, so there is time to pause. News (YearReport.interrupts: something expected of you, a finished or stalled project, a discovery, strangers, a death or birth) is shown with its year and makes that year last longer (NEWS_LINGER), but doesn't stop the years. Only a pop-up (a custom to decide or speak for) or a window the player opens holds the year; a life ending shows the life screen, and the years resume after it. A Project keeps its slot year after year until finished, set aside or stalled. Attending to the years, or letting them slip game.end_year(attended=...): a year the player steps through weighs slightly well (ATTENDED_KARMA); a year let pass with nothing taken up weighs slightly ill (DRIFTED_KARMA); a year let pass while working at something is neutral. Hidden like all karma. A coarse budget, no money at the start Budget is open-ended: food, hands (labour, renewed yearly) and regard (standing). The leader also draws on what is held in common. Exchange adds whatever form the people settle on (favours owed, wares, or tokens named for the land: shells, polished stones, beads). Costs for the common stores scale with the square root of the population. Start as the first band, not a civilisation game.new_game(): about 250 people in three camps, four known things (fire, stone edges, the old songs, a belief in the unseen whose form is random), and a first character the people have lately come to look to, for a reason drawn at random (bringing the hunters home through the snows, driving off a bear, settling a quarrel, finding water). Their predecessor gave way or died; nothing is inherited. Development like Civilization, but not prescribed discoveries.py: about 45 ideas in four domains (land, craft, lore, kin), in two eras. The first thirty or so (fire to planting, herding, a council, exchange, judgement) take 200–300 years; the later ones (LATER_IDEAS: the plough, copper, the wheel, walls, writing, tribute, those who fight, a market, the town...) need those first, and more people or trouble from outside, so they come over the next 150–200 years. One is available only when its prerequisites and circumstances hold (water nearby, grassland, hills, having met another people, an unfriendly neighbour, enough people). Insight comes from ordinary life every year, from someone working at it (the pursue project, one idea at a time), from chance events, and from other peoples. Walls and those who fight add defence, which makes raids rarer; once the people know what a town is, villages above TOWN_SIZE become towns. Ideas settle into forms Discoveries like customs of giving, planting, exchange, how leaders are chosen, or judgement have several forms with different effects (Form). The player chooses if they worked it out, or if they lead and it is a matter of custom. Otherwise the people's own inclinations decide. A choice strengthens its tags and weighs (lightly) on karma. Policy: customs can be settled anew A custom that has stood RESETTLE_AFTER years can be questioned (discoveries.customs). "Change how the people ..." is a people's work (reform) anyone respected can lead, help with or call others to; NPCs take it up mostly when the people are restless. When it is done the custom comes up again (GameState.due_choices, settled in game._settle_customs_anew): the player decides if they led the work or lead the people (and it is a matter of custom), otherwise speaks for a form; during a childhood the people's leanings decide, weighed by whoever called for it. discoveries.resettle undoes what the old form set once (a title, the rule of succession, a kind of exchange) before applying the new. Roles appear as the people change stations.py: leader, keeper, hunter, gatherer and maker at first; fisher, planter, herder and go-between appear with the discoveries that make them; hunters and gatherers grow rarer as herding and planting arrive. Rebirth draws from the roles that exist. Leadership is earned people.next_leader() chooses among the most respected (standing: regard, plus a little for elders), weighted toward the top, with no favour for the old leader's kin. While a leader lives, leadership_year() lets them give way when old or frail, or lets the people turn to someone who far outshines them. Anyone respected enough can also ask the people to follow them (the stand_forward deed); it may fail and cost standing. Later the form of "how the people decide" can change this: a council of elders, the strongest, or a lineage (the only form that ties leading to a family). Titles follow (nation.names). Other peoples; violence real but not the focus peoples.py: three other peoples, simulated coarsely. They grow, learn, meet you, share ideas, intermarry, and drift toward or away from you. Raids come as matters at hand: the leader is expected to seek redress; avenging is a harsh other answer, and anyone can help the struck camp rebuild. No armies. Karma only on the action layer Answers, cares and projects carry a hidden karma for their intention; an expected matter left unanswered subtracts EventInstance.penalty. Outcomes never touch it. Stored on Soul.karma, clamped to [-1, 1]. Lives of 20–50 turns, random death age Character.death_age is hidden: 16 + 20..50. Health can end a life sooner. Rebirth among the same people, random role game.begin_next_life(); childhood is fast-forwarded to age 16. Karma shapes conditions, not rank Carried-over inclinations, health, fortune, family stability, parents' warmth and which family you are born to. Half of it is spent doing so. Tendencies, felt not shown tendencies.py: choosing strengthens tags; setting a project aside weakens them. Inclinations change costs (±30%), and order and tint in the chooser. NPCs, same model simplified npc.py: tracked adults take on projects (elders and the leader always) and a deed a year by inclination, chosen from their cares and the answers to the matters the people's state raises (events.lasting_answers: hunger, quarrels, low stores, plenty); the leader also weighs the people's needs. Their deeds earn standing; only the leader's act on the people. No win condition The game runs until the player stops; it autosaves every year.

docs.title: Simulation modules
docs.text:
• state.py: dataclasses (GameState, Nation, Settlement, Neighbour, Project, Character, Soul, Budget, EventInstance) with to_dict/from_dict. The RNG state is saved too, so a loaded game plays on identically.
  • game.py: founding the people, the options for a year, the yearly loop and its interrupts, choosing a custom's form, death and the next life.
  • discoveries.py: the web of ideas, their forms and combined effects, yearly insight, and settling a custom anew.
  • projects.py: multi-year undertakings: working at ideas, ranging further, new camps, gathering places, store pits, fields, teaching, changing a custom, raising a child, apprentices, friendship and trade with other peoples...
  • actions.py: one-year deeds: lasting cares for each role, and the answers to matters at hand.
  • events.py: news and matters at hand (what lasts with the people's state, what comes by chance, what each role meets), their answers, yearly generation and resolution.
  • nation.py: each camp's food from its land (falling as it fills up), hunger and growth, what goes into the common stores, cohesion (which strains as the people grow), plenty and lore; each tracked family's means.
  • people.py: creating characters, families, ageing, marriage (sometimes to other peoples) and births, finding a new leader, keeping a few elders.
  • peoples.py, stations.py, tendencies.py, npc.py, world.py (cached map per seed, foraging values, place names), save.py (JSON).

docs.title: World generation
docs.text:
1. Perlin noise produces elevation and moisture grids of MAP_WIDTH × MAP_HEIGHT, sampled at each hex's true position and normalised to [0, 1]. The game seed fixes the map.
  2. Each value is bucketed by ELEVATION_THRESHOLDS / MOISTURE_THRESHOLDS; the pair names the biome (e.g. "Hill Forest").
  3. Resources are seeded from BIOME_RESOURCE_BASELINES; a tile's fertility (plant food, animal food, fresh water) drives harvests.

docs.title: Hex grid
docs.text: world/hexgrid.py is pure math for a pointy-top grid in "odd-r" offset coordinates: centres, exact pixel-to-tile picking, corners, neighbours, distance and fitting a map to a box. The map view dims land outside the people's range, outlines its border, marks camps (the leader's in saffron), outlines the player's home, and shows the ranges of other peoples once met.

docs.title: Concepts
docs.text: The design of Sankhara. How each part is built is in Architecture.

docs.title: Premise
docs.text:
A simulation of one people over many generations, played one life at a time. It is a nation builder in the spirit of Civilization's development (ideas that take years, plans that run until something interrupts them) and of Europa Universalis' leaders (people who are born, rule and die), but war and armies are not the point. Play is about food and stores, custom and government, and the people's ideas and culture.

Buddhist ideas (saṅkhāra, karma, rebirth) shape the mechanics but are never named or explained in the game, the README, the About text or any other description. Nothing says that there is no winning: the game simply runs until the player stops.

docs.title: The start
docs.text: The people begin as one small band, the first of their kind, a few hundred people at most (never more than about 1,500) in a few camps. They have fire, stone tools, names, a language, old songs and some belief in the unseen. There is no farming, trade, money, goods, cities or armies, and no settled way of choosing leaders.

docs.title: Development
docs.text:
Everything beyond that must be discovered, and nothing is prescribed to turn out as it did in the real world. Ideas form a web: each needs earlier ideas and the right circumstances (water nearby, grassland, game, having met another people, enough people). Insight comes from ordinary life, from someone working at an idea, from chance and from other peoples. A full web should take a few hundred years.

Many ideas are customs that settle into one of several forms with different effects: how giving works, what exchange uses (favours owed, wares, tokens of shell or stone, or none of these), how planting is done, how leaders are chosen, how wrongs are judged. Whoever worked an idea out, or the leader, chooses its form; when a custom is being settled anyone may speak for a form, and the respected are heard more. Otherwise the people's own inclinations decide.

Roles appear with the ideas that make them: leader, keeper of the songs, hunter, gatherer and maker at first; fisher, planter, herder, go-between and others later, while old ways grow rarer.

docs.title: A year
docs.text:
One turn is one year. The years run on a clock the player can pause or step through one at a time; each year lasts long enough to react. News (something expected of you, a work finished or stalled, a discovery, strangers, a death) is shown and lingers but does not stop the years. Only a pop-up asking the player to decide holds them.

The player acts as their current character, not as an abstract manager. They have:

  • Three slots of attention, all optional. Nothing is chosen for the player, and a whole life can pass with nothing taken up.
  • Their role's means: a coarse budget of a few kinds (food, hands, regard, and later whatever form of exchange the people settle on). The leader also draws on what is held in common; others on their family's.

docs.title: Attention
docs.text:
What a slot can hold comes in three groups, so there are only a dozen or so things to weigh in a year rather than a long menu:

  • Matters at hand: situations drawn from the people's real state and the year's events: a hungry camp, quarrels between named families, low stores or plenty, a stranger at the fire, a dying elder, a raid, talk that you should lead. Each role meets some of their own too (a hunter's share of a great kill, a keeper asked for the oldest songs, a maker asked for a blade). A matter offers two or three ways to meet it, which depend on the role: the leader can open the common stores to the hungry, a hunter can bring them meat, anyone can share their family's food or keep it close. Some matters are expected of the player; ignoring those weighs on the life, and any answer meets them. An answer is kept up for as long as the matter lasts.
  • The people's works: begin, help with, take up or call others to them (see below). A work holds its slot until it is finished, set aside or stalls, and then the slot is left free.
  • Your own: personal undertakings (raising a child, an apprentice, a following, a shelter) and lasting cares (your kin, your craft, the songs, the unseen), kept up until changed.

No choice is labelled good or bad. Taking more than your share, shaming someone, hoarding knowledge or driving a hard bargain never appear as items on a menu; they come up only as one way of meeting a real situation, next to the others. Regard is earned by serving the people: tending them, keeping their songs, and above all leading or helping a work of theirs to the end.

docs.title: Leading from anywhere
docs.text:
Most projects are the people's works: shared undertakings that outlive whoever began them. Anyone can begin one, help with one, take up one left unfinished, or call others to it; when the one leading it dies it passes on rather than ending. Together with speaking when customs are settled, this gives every role a clear, connected influence over the direction of the people, even though most lives will not be the leader's.

The thread between lives runs through these works: a new life opens with what was finished while the character grew up, and what is still unfinished and who carries it.

docs.title: Leadership
docs.text: In a society this young leadership is earned, not inherited. The people look to whoever is most respected; a leader may give way when old or frail, or be passed over for someone who far outshines them, and anyone respected enough can ask the people to follow them (and may fail). The first character leads for a random reason of their own (bringing the hunters home through the snows, settling a quarrel...), never because a parent died. Only if the people adopt a custom of lineage does leading pass through a family; a council of elders or the strongest are other forms.

docs.title: Events
docs.text: Each year brings events, some random and some from the people's state. They are not fair: outcomes can be unjust or pointless. Events are the main source of obligations, which ask something of the player and may have harsher alternative answers.

docs.title: Lives and rebirth
docs.text:
A life runs about 20 to 50 years from adulthood, with a hidden, random death age (health can end it sooner), so final decisions cannot be timed. A game is several hundred years and many lives.

On death the player is reborn among the same people, into a role drawn from those that exist. Rank is not a reward: every role has the same three slots, with different kinds and scope of influence (a leader's broad and slow, a fisher's local and immediate). Status says nothing about worth. The people the player shaped remain, and they may be born into the consequences.

docs.title: Karma
docs.text:
A hidden score in [-1, 1], never shown as a number or a word; only its effects are felt. It attaches to intention and choice, never to outcomes or to the budget: which answers, cares and works are taken up, which expected matters are ignored, which forms are chosen. Stepping through a year attentively weighs slightly well; letting a year slip by with nothing taken up weighs slightly ill.

At rebirth karma shapes the conditions within the new role, not the role itself: mostly the inclinations carried over, and to a lesser degree health, fortune, family stability and the warmth of parents.

docs.title: Tendencies (saṅkhāra)
docs.text: A life's habitual choices become the next life's default impulses. They are never shown as labels or a character sheet, only felt: some choices cost less, come first or are tinted as tempting; others carry friction. The nudge is mild to moderate, always overridable at a small cost, and consistent enough to be learned. Repetition strengthens a tendency, acting against it weakens it, and the pattern at death carries over.

docs.title: Other people
docs.text:
NPCs follow the same model, simplified. The leader, elders and people near the player or in power are tracked in detail; the rest are handled statistically.

Other peoples share the land. They grow, learn, meet the player's people, share ideas, intermarry, and drift toward or away from them.

docs.title: Violence
docs.text: Violence is real and should be present, but never the focus. For now it comes as raids from other peoples, answered by seeking redress or, more harshly, by revenge. There are no armies; any form of organised violence must be discovered like everything else.

docs.title: Ahead
docs.text:
• M2: policy and government, and more development.
  • M3: detailed NPCs, relationships and politics.
  • Becoming non-human is out of the main game (perhaps an easter egg).

docs.title: Play-test notes
docs.text: New feedback goes here; it is folded into the sections above once built.

docs.title: Development
docs.text:
Requires uv. The project is pinned to Python 3.12 (.python-version); uv will download it if needed.

uv sync                     # create .venv with runtime + dev dependencies
uv run pre-commit install   # run ruff and basic checks on every commit

docs.title: Common commands
docs.text: Task Command Run the game uv run sankhara Tests (with coverage) uv run pytest Lint uv run ruff check . Format uv run ruff format . All pre-commit hooks uv run pre-commit run --all-files Docs preview uv run --group docs mkdocs serve

docs.title: Tests
docs.text: Tests live in tests/, mirroring the package layout (test_core/, test_world/, …). tests/conftest.py sets KIVY_NO_ARGS so Kivy doesn't consume pytest's arguments. UI tests need a display; CI runs them under xvfb-run.

docs.title: CI
docs.text: GitHub Actions runs lint and tests on every push and pull request (.github/workflows/ci.yml), and publishes these docs to GitHub Pages on pushes to main (.github/workflows/docs.yml).
